Class AetherisNotebookPanel.ViewFind

java.lang.Object
org.aetheris.swing.AetherisNotebookPanel.ViewFind
Enclosing class:
AetherisNotebookPanel
private final class AetherisNotebookPanel.ViewFind extends Object
The class ViewFind is the find bar for one View window. The bar holds the reply area, the text field, the count label, and the match spans. A match is a pair of character indexes in that reply. The matches live in this reply. The canvas search stays on the canvas. The brown painter is color 0x6b5a1e. The amber painter for the current match is color 0xf9a825. The constant CAP is 2000. The current index starts at -1. The more flag starts false. A caller passes the reply area to the constructor. A caller then calls install(JDialog) on the View dialog. The bar stays hidden until Ctrl-F shows it. The type keeps at most CAP spans. A further match sets more and is not stored. The type does not change the reply text.

  • Constructor Details

    • ViewFind

      private ViewFind(JTextArea area)
      The constructor builds the hidden find bar for one reply area. The field is 24 columns wide. The field tooltip says that typing highlights every match in this reply. The same tooltip says that Ctrl-F finds the next match. The same tooltip says that Esc closes this bar. The count label starts as one space. The previous button is labeled ^. That button calls step(int) with -1. The next button is labeled v. That button calls step(int) with 1. A change in the field document calls retarget(). The bar starts invisible.
      Parameters:
      area - The area is the reply text this bar searches.

  • Method Details

    • install

      private void install(JDialog dialog)
      The method binds Ctrl-F and Esc on the dialog while that window is focused. Ctrl-F is stored as aetheris-view-find. Esc is stored as aetheris-view-find-esc. Ctrl-F runs onFindKey(). Esc hides the bar when the bar is visible. Esc then asks the reply area for focus. Esc does nothing to the reply when the bar is already hidden.
      Parameters:
      dialog - The dialog is the View window that owns this bar.

    • onFindKey

      private void onFindKey()
      The method handles Ctrl-F. A hidden bar is shown, and the method returns. A null field is treated as empty. An empty field asks for focus, and the method returns. Any other field text calls step(int) with 1.

    • showBar

      private void showBar()
      The method makes the bar visible. A parent of the bar is revalidated and repainted. A missing parent is left alone. The method then calls retarget(). The method asks the field for focus. A field that already holds text selects all of that text.

    • hideBar

      private void hideBar()
      The method hides the bar. The method removes every highlight from the reply. The method clears the spans. The current index becomes -1. The more flag becomes false. The count label becomes one space. The caret is placed at the selection start, which drops the selection. A parent of the bar is revalidated and repainted. A missing parent is left alone.

    • retarget

      private void retarget()
      The method rebuilds the match list from the field text. The spans are cleared first. more becomes false. The current index becomes -1. A null field is treated as empty. An empty field removes every highlight. An empty field sets the count label to one space and returns. A null reply is treated as empty. The search calls indexOfIgnoreCase(String, String, int) and steps forward by the needle length. Each kept match stores the start index and the end index. The search stops when the list reaches CAP. That stop sets more. No spans leaves the highlights clear and the count as none. One or more spans selects index 0 and calls applyHighlights().

    • step

      private void step(int dir)
      The method moves the current match by dir. A positive dir moves toward the end before wrapping. A negative dir moves toward the start before wrapping. An empty span list returns without a change. A current index below 0 becomes 0. Any other index adds dir. An index past the last span wraps to 0. An index below 0 wraps to the last span. The method then calls applyHighlights().
      Parameters:
      dir - The dir is the signed count added to the current match index.

    • applyHighlights

      private void applyHighlights()
      The method removes every highlight and paints the stored spans. The current span uses the amber painter. Every other span uses the brown painter. A BadLocationException from one span skips that span and continues. A current index outside the list calls paintCount() and returns. The caret moves to the start of the current span. The current span becomes the selection. The method scrolls that start into view when the area can map it. A BadLocationException from that map calls paintCount() and returns. The method ends by calling paintCount().

    • paintCount

      private void paintCount()
      The method writes the count label. A null field is treated as empty. An empty field sets the label to one space and returns. No spans sets the label to none and returns. Any other list sets the label to the 1-based current index, then / , then the span count. A true more flag appends + to that label.

    • indexOfIgnoreCase

      private static int indexOfIgnoreCase(String hay, String needle, int from)
      The method returns the next case-insensitive match of needle in hay. The search starts at from. Each index uses String.regionMatches with the ignore-case flag true. The needle length is the match length. No match returns -1.
      Parameters:
      hay - The hay is the reply text.
      needle - The needle is the field text to find.
      from - The from is the first index that may start a match.
      Returns:
      The method returns the match index, or -1 when no match remains.
